comments.author: @leechumbley5440
comments.text: Marrakesh is the epitome of the exotic. One sees a snake charmer playing a languorous flute melody as a cobra sways, a crowd surrounds a bard with a lute singing ancient folk tales, a trained monkey dances.  Casablanca girls telling their beaux “Inta kabidy“ you are my liver.   In addition to Fez, Marrakesh as well has crowded vats for leather making. In fact, the very words in French for leather (maroquin) and leather-making (maroquinerie) reflect Marocco’s reputation for fine leather handbags, wallets, gloves, shoes, and bookcovers. Fascinating to learn that Meknes began as an Almoravid fortress in the 11th century. Modern genetic studies have shown that Moulai Ismail’s Y-chromosome is very widespread – like Jenghis Khan’s – quite the lad. He took Tangier, putting paid to Great Britain’s imperial plans for Morocco in the 17th century. How extraordinary to see Rousani, near Sijilmasa, which once had huge amounts of gold - the ‘Fort Knox’ of the Almoravid Caliphate of combined Morocco and Islamic Spain.  Much of Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey was filmed in Morocco. Aït Benhaddou was the burning city of Troy, Essaouira's Atlantic beaches for the Trojan Horse discovery, Marrakech for palace interiors. Near Tangier is the ancient Roman city of Volubolis, where Cleopatra’s daughter Selene once ruled as Queen of Mauritania. This was a wonderful trip. Thank you.
